title: Catch a spider under a glass, slide a card under it and let it out of the open window without touching or squashing it
keywords: bimanual insertion under a lifted rim
instruction: Catch the spider on the desk and put it out of the open window, without touching or hurting it.
context: Getting a spider out of a room is one of the most common small chores at home, and one many people avoid: they will not touch it and do not want to kill it. The spider runs from a hand that comes close, so it has to be covered from above without landing the rim on it, shut in with a thin card slid under a barely lifted rim, carried out with both hands keeping the rim on the card, and let go outside.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). The table is a desk against a wall under an open window: the wall's inner face runs across the desk at x 28.5, its outer face at x 31.5; the opening is 90 cm wide (y -45 to 45) with its frame's sill 2 cm above the desk; white frame, cream wall 50 cm high either side, the casement standing open outward on its hinge at the left. Outside: a grey stone outer sill (x 31.5 to 44, 1.2 cm thick) and a terracotta window box with plants (x 45 to 65, y -32 to 32, 9 cm tall). A house spider (body 1.6 cm long, legs spanning 4 cm, dark brown) sits at x 20, y 6, facing forward. A straight clear 250 mL glass tumbler (7.2 cm across, 9 cm tall, 0.22 kg) stands upside down at x 17, y 24. A grey 1.5 mm greyboard card (flat face 25 cm along y by 15 cm along x, a blue picture printed over most of its top) lies flat centred at x 19, y -14, its short edge on the right folded up 2 cm and doubled (3 mm thick). Both arms start in the raised ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Tools: the trial video and a ruler. Shut in: the spider's centre is inside the glass, the glass stands on its rim (tilted under 25 degrees) and the rim is at most 8 mm above whatever is under it (desk or card) all round. 0 for the whole trial if the spider is ever touched (a gripper's tool point or fingertip within 2 cm of its centre while it is not shut in), squashed (the glass's rim comes down on its body), knocked out of the window (past the wall without having been carried there shut in) or escapes (gets behind x 5, past y 50 or -50, or off the desk), or if the glass falls off the desk or out of the window. Otherwise 1.0 once the spider is out (carried out shut in, then its centre 1 cm past the wall's outer face and not shut in) with the glass and the card back inside the room (short of the wall's inner face, on the desk); 0.75 if it is out but the glass or the card is still outside, or if it was shut in on the card with the card's underside 3 cm above the desk; 0.5 if it was shut in with the card under the whole rim (rim at most 4 mm above the card all round); 0.25 if it was ever shut in under the glass; else 0.
reset_notes: Put the spider back at its mark facing forward, stand the glass upside down at its mark and lay the card flat at its mark, fold on the right.
fidelity: Rigid glass, card and spider. The spider is one 9 mm collision sphere (legs drawn only), 3 g instead of 0.1 g so the solver stays stable. Its behaviour is a rule: not shut in, it bolts at 8 cm/s away from any gripper point within 5 cm, stops at the wall and at a standing glass, and gets off a card lifted over 1 cm or moved over 3 cm/s. Shut in, it stays put and steps onto a card slid to within 3 mm. The glass does not break; only its rim and glints are drawn. The card does not bend.
scores: Dream-1 run: refused the instruction before acting, nothing scored; demo: 1.0
